task.description: Idiom/scope-creep/correctness gate on ELIXIR-DEV's raw-text splice implementation for ISS-0442 (option (b) of the approved design), before TEST-DESIGNER writes the committed regression suite. Independently run the full test suite to completion in the foreground (ELIXIR-DEV disclosed 3 failed attempts at ~590s each), independently reproduce AC1's diff-size claim, verify the implementation against the design's §2.2 scan algorithm, and form an independent judgment on the test-coverage gap ELIXIR-DEV's own mutation testing surfaced (removing the depth==1 guard survives all 43 existing tests).

result.summary:
FULL SUITE (ran to completion in the foreground myself, blocking on the actual OS process across three sequential 10-minute `tail --pid=<pid> -f /dev/null` waits totalling ~26 minutes wall clock, since this sandbox's per-tool-call timeout cap of 600s is shorter than the suite's ~1542s runtime -- I did not accept ELIXIR-DEV's 3x-timeout non-result as sufficient): `mix test` -> 'Finished in 1542.2 seconds (19.0s async, 1523.2s sync)' / 'Result: 3201/3203 passed (6/6 properties, 3195/3197 tests), 21 excluded' / 'Failed: 2 tests'. Re-ran just the 2 failures via `mix test --failed` (0.4s): both are `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest` ('a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...' and 'a matching rust pin reports OK...'), both failing with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` at test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs:69. Confirmed via `which rustc` (exit 1, not found) that this sandbox has no Rust toolchain installed at all -- a pre-existing environment gap with zero relationship to lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex or this diff (different Mix task, different test file, fails identically on `main` for the same reason). Ran the scoped file separately for a clean signal: `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 9.4 seconds' / 'Result: 43 passed', matching ELIXIR-DEV's own reported number exactly. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean, no output, exit 0. Verdict: full suite is GREEN modulo a pre-existing, unrelated, environment-only gap (no rustc in this sandbox) that also fails on main and is out of scope for this change.

AC1 INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION (not copied from ELIXIR-DEV's report -- built and run separately, in a scratch dir, calling `rewrite_top_level_status!/3` directly via `mix run --no-start`): copied the same real fixture (handoffs/WF03-ISS0392-20260901/step-00-git-setup.json, 48 lines, top-level status COMPLETED at line 12, nested result.status PASS at line 32, trailing newline present), mutated top-level status to PASS (reproducing the exact PASS/PASS collision), then fixed PASS->COMPLETED. Result: `diff -u` against the ORIGINAL file is EMPTY (0 lines) -- the round-tripped file is byte-identical to the pre-mutation original, a stronger check than a line-count comparison. `diff -u` against the PASS-mutated intermediate shows exactly one changed line (`-  "status": "PASS",` / `+  "status": "COMPLETED",`). Nested `result.status` at line 32 confirmed untouched (still PASS) both by grep and by the empty full-file diff. Trailing newline confirmed identical (`xxd` on both files' last byte: `0a`). Separately built and tested an escape/embedded-structure fixture (`{"status": "PASS", "note": "escaped \"quote\" and brace { } inside string", "arr": ["a", "b"], "result": {"status": "PASS"}}`, no trailing newline): after fixing PASS->COMPLETED, only the top-level status token changed; the embedded escaped quote, the embedded literal braces inside the string value, the inline array `["a", "b"]`, and the nested result.status were all byte-identical to the pre-fix version, and the file still had no trailing newline afterward. AC1 and the design's nested-collision and byte-identical-passthrough claims are independently confirmed, not just re-derived from ELIXIR-DEV's report.

DESIGN CONFORMANCE (`git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904 -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex`, full read): `write_json!/2` removed, its one call site now calls `rewrite_top_level_status!(path, raw, to)` using the `raw` binding already in `autofix_file/1`'s own `with`-clause -- no second file read, matching §2.0/§2.1 exactly. `rewrite_top_level_status!/3` and `splice_top_level_status/2` match the specified signatures exactly (`@spec`s present). The scan is implemented as recursive-descent binary pattern matching (`scan_for_status/4` et al.) in the same style as the module's existing `find_dir_flag/1`, per the design's explicit implementation note -- no numeric byte-offset slicing anywhere. Depth tracking increments/decrements on `{`/`[`/`}`/`]` only when NOT inside a string (string boundaries are resolved first via `consume_json_string/1` before the depth-changing clauses ever see the characters inside a string value, since `scan_for_status`'s `<<?", _::binary>>` clause intercepts before the generic character clause) -- confirmed structurally in the diff, not just claimed, and confirmed empirically by the escape/embedded-brace fixture above. Key-vs-value decided by the syntactic colon-lookahead rule (`key_follows?/1` + `skip_ws/1`), not alternating parity, matching §2.2 exactly. Last-key-wins implemented via `new_best` overwriting `best` on every depth-1 "status" match found, keeping the scan going rather than stopping at the first hit, matching §2.2 step 2 exactly. The internal-invariant-violation path uses a plain `raise/1` with a descriptive message, not `Mix.raise/1` -- ELIXIR-DEV's documented judgment call, consistent with the design's own reasoning in §4 (not user-facing) and with this reviewer's own read of the module's existing convention (`Mix.raise/1` is used elsewhere only for user-facing usage errors like a malformed `--dir` flag). No fallback to the old whole-document re-encode on that path, matching §2.1's explicit prohibition. `Jason.encode!/1` is used only on the single scalar `new_status` string, never on a whole map, matching §2.2 step 4. No new dependency, no mix.lock change (confirmed via `git diff --stat`: only lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, the design doc, docs/issues/ISS-0442.yaml, and this run's own handoff/registry files changed -- test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs is untouched, correctly left for TEST-DESIGNER).

UNCHANGED-BRANCH VERIFICATION (explicit diff, not taken on faith): `autofix_file/1`'s `case Map.get(data, "status") do` block shows exactly one line changed -- the fixed branch's action (`data |> Map.put(...) |> write_json!(path)` -> `rewrite_top_level_status!(path, raw, to)`); the `"FAIL"` branch, the legal-but-unmapped branch, the missing/non-string branch, and the already-legal `:skip` branch (via the outer `status when is_binary(status) and status in @legal_statuses -> :skip` clause, itself untouched) are byte-identical to main, same match patterns, same `{:refused, ...}` tuples, same reason strings. `run/1`'s `if autofix? do run_autofix(files) else :ok end` guard and every line of `run_autofix/1`, `resolve_dir/1`, `guard_empty_scope/2`, `lint_file/2`, and the H1-H6/H-SIZE checks do not appear anywhere in the diff at all -- confirmed by `git diff --stat` showing this file's diff is +183/-10 lines, all localized to the single case-branch line plus the new private-function block appended after `autofix_file/1`, with nothing above line 417 or in `run/1`/`run_autofix/1` touched.

SCOPE / IDIOM: no new module, behaviour, macro, or dependency. All new code is private helper functions inside the existing `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffs` module (two `def`s matching the design's public-shape spec, the rest `defp`), using plain binary pattern matching -- the idiomatic Elixir style already established in this exact module (`find_dir_flag/1`), not a crutch. No `GenServer`/`gen_statem`/supervision concerns apply -- this is a synchronous Mix task with no process/state-machine component, so idiom questions 1-2 (per-instance gen_statem, InstanceSupervisor isolation) are not implicated. Question 3 (type-safety gap): the new code operates entirely on raw binaries and returns `String.t()`/`:ok`; the `{prefix_before_value, old_value_raw, suffix_after_value}` tuple used as `best`'s shape is an internal, single-function-scoped accumulator, not a public data shape a struct/Ecto.Enum would meaningfully replace -- no type-safety gap worth filing here, unlike ISS-0442's transition-domain siblings. Question 4 (scope creep): none -- the diff is exactly the design's two named functions and their private helpers, nothing built ahead of what this fix needs (no generic "JSON patcher" abstraction, no reusable splice library exposed beyond this module's own private scope).

SECURITY-REVIEWER SKIP: independently re-checked against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's own criteria rather than taking ELIXIR-DEV's word. INV-1 (tenant data isolation) applies to Ecto schema/migration changes reading/writing business data through `:prefix`-scoping -- this change touches neither; `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` reads/writes plain files under `handoffs/`, a dev-tooling directory, via `File.read/1`/`File.write!/2`, with no Repo/Ecto/tenant-schema involvement anywhere in the diff. INV-2 (server-side field authorization) applies to API response shaping -- not applicable, no route/controller/view touched. No other invariant in the file (INV-3 through INV-8, skimmed for applicability) references file I/O, dev tooling, or CI-adjacent scripts. Skip is correct.

COVERAGE-GAP JUDGMENT (ELIXIR-DEV's issues[0], mutation 2 in their report): independently reproduced the mechanism myself before ruling on it -- copied the module to a scratch file, renamed it, removed only the `depth == 1 and` clause from `handle_string_token/5`'s guard (`if depth == 1 and key_follows?(after_string) do` -> `if key_follows?(after_string) do`), compiled the mutant standalone via `Code.compile_file/1` (not touching the tracked file, so the concurrent full-suite run in progress at the time was not disturbed), and ran it against the exact PASS/PASS collision fixture (top-level `status: \"PASS\"`, nested `result.status: \"PASS\"`). Result: the mutant left the top-level status WRONG (still `\"PASS\"`, never fixed) and corrupted the nested `result.status` to `\"COMPLETED\"` instead -- exactly the ISS-0442 collision the whole design exists to prevent, now reintroduced by a single-token guard deletion. Separately confirmed via `grep` that `test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs`'s one fixture combining both nesting levels (`T-AUTOFIX-DOES-NOT-TOUCH-NESTED-RESULT-STATUS`, line 652) uses an already-legal top-level `COMPLETED`, which hits the `:skip` branch and never reaches `rewrite_top_level_status!/3` at all -- so no existing test exercises the splice code on a file that also has a nested `status` key. My own judgment, formed from directly reproducing the corruption rather than from ELIXIR-DEV's description of it: this is not an advisory-tier observation. The `depth == 1` guard is the single mechanism that makes ISS-0442's fix correct rather than merely differently-shaped, and its removal currently produces a silent, undetected wrong-field write with all 43 existing tests green. I am escalating this from ELIXIR-DEV's ADVISORY framing to a REQUIRED, named condition of this PASS -- see acceptance_criteria_for_next_step below. TEST-DESIGNER may not treat it as optional.

No BLOCKER. PASS.
acceptance_criteria_for_next_step: REQUIRED, not optional: TEST-DESIGNER must add a regression fixture combining a top-level FIXABLE status (one of PASS/COMPLETE/DONE, i.e. one that reaches the splice branch, not an already-legal status that hits :skip) with a nested result.status also present in the same file, matching ISSUE-FIXER's originally demonstrated collision shape. The test must assert BOTH: (a) the rewritten file's top-level status is corrected to the mapped value, and (b) the nested result.status is byte-identical to its pre-fix value. This is the one mutation (removing the `depth == 1` guard in handle_string_token/5) that this reviewer independently reproduced as surviving all 43 existing tests while silently corrupting the wrong field -- it must become load-bearing, mutation-killing coverage, not left as the advisory ELIXIR-DEV's own handoff proposed.

Standard §4 fixtures from the design doc (inline single-line array untouched post-fix; no-trailing-newline file stays without one post-fix) should also be added -- not a hard blocker on their own, but expected alongside the required fixture above since this reviewer independently reproduced both behaviors and found them correct.
